# React Component Convention

File naming, single export, props, folder structure, handler naming. Vocabulary comes from [vocabulary-convention.md](../../core/vocabulary-convention.md); how a name is assembled is in [naming-convention.md](../../core/naming-convention.md).

## Scope

Applies to every React component file.

Does **not** apply to:

- The app entry file, the route table, and provider files — those are wiring, not components, and keep named exports so a registry can compose them.
- Generated component files.

## File Naming

- Component files: **PascalCase**, file name = component name → `RoutineForm.tsx`, `AppCard.tsx`
- Pages: `<Action><Domain>Page.tsx` for a task, plural `<Domains>Page.tsx` for a collection, `<Area>Page.tsx` for an area → `EditRoutinePage.tsx`, `RoutinesPage.tsx`, `SettingsPage.tsx`
- Layouts: `*Layout.tsx`, route shells only → `DashboardLayout.tsx`
- Modals: `<Action><Domain>Modal.tsx` — verb first, then the domain → `CollectFeedbackModal.tsx`
- Sibling non-JSX files keep `.ts` — `constants.ts`, `helpers.ts`

```tsx
// WRONG — kebab-case
routine-form.tsx
settings-page.tsx
```

## Component Naming

- **A Page or Modal is a task** → `<Action><Domain>` (`EditRoutinePage`, `SwapProductModal`). A collection page is the plural noun (`RoutinesPage`), never `…ListPage`.
- **Every other component is a thing** → `<Domain><Role>` (`RoutineForm`, `StepReviewItem`), with the role taken from this list:

  `…Layout` (route shell rendering an outlet, nothing else) · `…Card` (titled block) · `…Panel` (region with its own actions) · `…Item` (one element of a rendered list) · `…Actions` (button group) · `…Form` · `…Preview` · `…Badge` · `…Label` · `…Button` · `…Picker` / `…Calendar` · `…Provider`

  Never `Row`, `Entry`, `Box`, `Section`, `Wrapper`, `View`, `Screen`, `Container`.
- **Unique within the feature**, private sub-components included — qualify by context instead of reusing (`StepFormItem` / `StepReviewItem`, not two `StepItem`).
- **`Layout` is a route shell only.** A reusable card frame is a `…Card`.
- **Hooks are not components** — `useX.ts` (camelCase, file = hook name), named export, `.ts` unless it renders JSX, return type `{X}Result`.

```tsx
// WRONG
RoutineListPage.tsx                                    // …ListPage
RoutinePreviewPage.tsx                                 // domain before action on a task page
RoutineForm/StepItem.tsx + RoutineReview/StepItem.tsx  // same name twice
WidgetCardLayout.tsx                                   // Layout outside a route shell
```

## Single Component Per File

- Each file exports **exactly one** component as **default export**.
- The file exports nothing else — no named exports, no helper types, no constants, no re-exported sub-components.
- Sub-components, constants and helpers stay private to the file. When they grow, promote the component to a folder.

```tsx
// CORRECT — exactly one default export
interface RoutineFormProps { ... }

const statusOptions = [ ... ];

export default function RoutineForm({ ... }: RoutineFormProps) { ... }

// WRONG — named export
export function RoutineForm({ ... }: RoutineFormProps) { ... }

// WRONG — multiple exports from a component file
export default function RoutineForm({ ... }: RoutineFormProps) { ... }
export const statusOptions = [ ... ];
export type { RoutineFormProps };
```

One export per file is what makes the import list readable: every import line names a component, and nothing has to be traced back to find out what it is.

## Props

- Props interface name: `{ComponentName}Props`, defined at the **top of the file**, after imports and before any constants.
- Use `interface`, not `type`.
- Destructure props at the function signature.
- Optional props use `?:`.
- Callback props use the `on*` prefix.
- The props interface is **not exported** — it stays private to the component file.

```tsx
// CORRECT
interface RoutineFormProps {
  mode: 'create' | 'edit';
  form: UseFormReturn<RoutineFormData>;
  isSaving?: boolean;
  onSave: () => void;
  onCancel: () => void;
}

export default function RoutineForm({ mode, form, isSaving, onSave, onCancel }: RoutineFormProps) { ... }

// WRONG — props typed inline, destructured in the body
export default function RoutineForm(props: { mode: 'create' | 'edit' }) {
  const { mode } = props;
}

// WRONG — no Props suffix, or exported
interface RoutineForm { ... }
export interface RoutineFormProps { ... }
```

## Handler Naming

Two distinct namespaces — keep them paired.

- **Callback props**: `on*` → `onClick`, `onClose`, `onSave`, `onSubmit`.
- **Local handler definitions**: `handleOn*` → `handleOnClick`, `handleOnClose`, `handleOnSave`.
- When a local handler wraps a prop callback, the names pair: prop `onSave` → local `handleOnSave`.
- The subject comes before the event — `onRoleChange` / `handleOnRoleChange`, never `handleOnChangeRole`. A callback that triggers an action names its verb — `onViewPerformance`, not `onPerformance`.

```tsx
// CORRECT
export default function SettingsPanel({ onSave, onClose }: SettingsPanelProps) {
  const handleOnSave = () => {
    onSave(collectFormData());
  };

  const handleOnClose = () => {
    if (confirm('Discard changes?')) {
      onClose();
    }
  };

  return <form onSubmit={handleOnSave}>…</form>;
}

// WRONG — local handler missing `On`, so it no longer pairs with its prop
const handleSave = () => { ... };

// WRONG — prop callback without `on*`
interface SettingsPanelProps {
  save: () => void;
  handleClose: () => void;
}
```

`handleOn*` rather than `handle*` exists so that the local name and the prop name differ by exactly one prefix. Reading `onSave` you know a `handleOnSave` may exist; reading `handleSave` you have to search.

This is a **UI** convention. A backend method that handles an inbound event is `handle<Event>` with no `On` ([logging-convention.md](../../core/logging-convention.md)).

## Folder Structure for Complex Components

A component lives in a **single file** by default. Promote it to a folder when any of these is true:

1. It has ≥1 sub-component worth its own file.
2. Its constants or helpers exceed ~30 lines.
3. The single file would exceed ~200 lines.

```
ComponentName/
├── index.tsx           // main component (default export)
├── SubComponent.tsx    // sub-components, each its own default export
├── constants.ts        // used only inside this folder
└── helpers.ts          // pure helpers used only inside this folder
```

The main component goes in `index.tsx`, so importers write `import ComponentName from './ComponentName'`. `constants.ts` / `helpers.ts` may export named values, consumed only by files **inside the same folder**.

A folder of small sibling components that ship together — a field-wrapper set, a picker and its panel — is a different shape: each file its own default export, plus a barrel re-exporting them. Use it for a shared library folder, not for a feature component.

## Co-location of Constants & Helpers

| Scope of reuse                              | Location                                            |
| ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| One single-file component                   | inline at the top of the file, before the component |
| One folder-based component and its children | sibling `constants.ts` / `helpers.ts` in the folder |
| Several components in one feature           | the feature's own `constants/` / `helpers/`         |
| Across features                             | the shared `common/` equivalent                     |

Never export a constant or helper from a component file. If another component needs it, move it up to the closest shared location — that move is the signal that it was never component-local.

Component-scoped closures that capture state or form handles stay inline in the component body. They are handlers, not helpers.

## Page / Layout / Component

| Role                  | Filename      | Responsibility                                                                 |
| --------------------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Page**              | `*Page.tsx`   | Route-level. Owns data fetching, mutations, navigation and form orchestration. |
| **Layout**            | `*Layout.tsx` | Route shell — navigation, header. Renders the outlet and nothing else.         |
| **Feature component** | `*.tsx`       | Presentational and feature-specific. No data fetching, no navigation.          |
| **Shared component**  | `*.tsx`       | Globally reusable. No feature-specific knowledge.                              |

Pages own the query and mutation hooks and the submit wiring. Feature components accept callbacks (`onSave`, `onCancel`) instead of triggering mutations themselves — which is what makes them renderable in a test, a story, and a second page.

A component must not import a Page or a Layout.

## NEVER Do

- Use kebab-case for a component filename.
- Use a named export for a component — always `export default`.
- Export anything besides the component itself from a component file.
- Put the props interface inside the component body, after the component, or in a separate file.
- Name the props interface anything other than `{ComponentName}Props`, or export it.
- Use a callback-prop name without `on*`, or a local handler without `handleOn*`.
- Put the event before the subject (`handleOnChangeRole`), or give an action prop no verb (`onPerformance`).
- Leave a single-file component over ~200 lines or with multiple inline sub-components.
- Export constants or helpers from a component file.
- Put a Page inside the components folder, or a presentational component in the pages folder.
- Put logic in a Layout — layouts are route shells.
- Name a task page `<Domain><Action>Page`, or a collection page `…ListPage`.
- Use a role suffix outside the list above.
- Reuse a component name already taken in the feature.
- Fetch data or navigate from a feature component.
